points: 始める marks the beginning of an action; 終わる marks its completion.
Reports a request, instruction, prohibition, or advice given to someone.
Content quoted or described as a noun
Packages a statement as the content of a noun such as こと, 話, or 文字.
Think or expect that something is probably true
A tentative expectation. Nouns and な-adjectives use だろうと思う.
Aく／Aじゃ／Nじゃ＋なさそうだ
Negative appearance or impression: 辛くなさそう, 大変じゃなさそう.
Often describes a discovery or unexpected state noticed after an action; the result is often past tense.
Expresses degree, often with an unusually strong result or state.
Change or movement away / toward the speaker’s viewpoint
いく can show movement away or change continuing into the future; くる can show movement toward, change emerging, or an action continuing from the past.
Shows that an action continues over time.
If it’s about … / if you’re going to …
Introduces a relevant topic or condition and often leads to advice or a suggestion.
Casual form used to introduce or explain a person, place, or thing.
Vさせてもらう／Vさせてくれる
Causative + てもらう／くれる expresses permission received or granted.
Causative-passive: someone is made to do something, often unwillingly. Godan verbs may contract to ～される.
Show signs of feeling or wanting
Used to describe observable feelings or desires in another person (and sometimes animals).
A second event occurs immediately after the first, often unexpectedly.
Marks the sudden beginning of an action or change.
Try or intend to; refuse to
Describes an attempt or intention; negative form can criticize a refusal to act. ～ようとしたら often introduces an interruption.
Describes an occasional action or event.
Leave someone in a state or allow an action to continue, sometimes after instructing them.
Passive + しまう often conveys that another person’s action inconvenienced or upset the speaker.
によって can indicate means or agent; による modifies a following noun.
Marks the target or subject of an attitude, action, policy, or discussion.
Because of; for the sake of
Can state a cause or a purpose; context distinguishes the two.
Formal counter expression, e.g. 一人につき三つ (three per person).
Says something happens as expected, described, or instructed.
Indicates a medium, intermediary, or means of gaining experience.
Uses a noun as a comparison or example.
Introduces a source of information, often followed by そうだ, らしい, or ということだ.
Plain form＋ということだ／とのことだ
I heard / it is said that
Reports information or a message heard from another source.
Marks the topic of study, information, or discussion.
Casual contractions: てる・とく・ちゃう・なきゃ
Examples: 見ている→見てる; 読んでおく→読んどく; 忘れてしまう→忘れちゃう; 読まなければ→読まなきゃ.
Casual shortening of なければいけない; context may omit いけない.
Casual way to check or recall information, often something previously known.
At sentence end, ～たりして can make a light, speculative guess. It is not a general past-form + りして rule.
Colloquial equivalent of でも／ても in concessive statements.
Strongly asserts that something is certain or obvious.
Isn’t it …? / It is …, isn’t it?
Casual confirmation or assertion; intonation and context affect the meaning.
Colloquial topic marker or quotation marker, depending on context.
Casual expression of impression, inference, or similarity.
ば／ければ／なら＋良かった
I wish I had … / It would have been good if …
Expresses regret or hindsight about a different condition or choice.
N＋ばかり means mostly/nothing but; Vて＋ばかりいる suggests repeatedly doing one thing, often critically. Vた＋ばかり means just did.
Nの・V・A＋ようだ／ように／ようなN
Forms comparison or impression; ような modifies a noun and ように modifies an action or description.
Highlights an expected item and adds another item.
Not as … as; not to the extent …
Says the degree is less than expected or less than a comparison point.
Expresses substitution, exchange, or a trade-off.
A state remains as it is, or an expected action has not been done.
Verb ます-stem (連用形) to connect clauses
The ます-stem can connect actions or clauses in concise written language: 実施し、まとめる. It is not the て-form.
Vる・Vている・Vた＋ところに／へ／を／で
A person arrives, an event occurs, or an action is observed at a particular moment; the particle depends on the sentence.
Means doing something to completion, or being thoroughly in a state such as 疲れ切る.
Plain form・Aな・Nの＋おかげで
Attributes a positive result to a person, condition, or action.
Time expression＋を通じて／を通して
Says something continues or is true across the entire time period.
Vませんか／A・Nじゃないですか
A question inviting the listener’s agreement or opinion.
というと／と言えば／と言ったら
Introduces an association, representative example, or topic that comes to mind.
Vる＋べきだ／べきではない
Expresses a strong sense of what is right or advisable. するべき and すべき are both used; すべき is more compact.
Shows how something is evaluated from a person’s point of view.
Describes two changes that increase together; for example, 勉強すればするほど.
Can identify a cause, means, or agent. Use context to tell which relationship is intended.
Plain form・Aな・Nである＋ばかりでなく～も
Adds a second point to the first; the structure can emphasize both.
Describes something that happens each time an event occurs.
Expresses an expectation based on a reason or evidence.
Formal way to state a condition and its result, often in service or business settings.
Plain form・Aな・Nの＋ようなら
A tentative condition based on the situation or an impression.
A change begins / comes into view
Can describe a new change emerging or becoming noticeable, as well as movement toward the speaker.
Plain form・Aな・Nな＋もので／ものですから
Gives a reason or excuse, often with a softer explanatory tone. Casual forms: もんで／もんだから.
Casual forms of など; can suggest an example, soften a suggestion, or express emotion depending on context.
Softens an opinion or prediction, often in polite or business conversation.
Vる・Vている・Vない＋うちに
A change happens during an ongoing state or before that state ends.
The speaker feels little time has passed since the action, regardless of exact elapsed time.
ば／ければ／なら＋いいのに
Expresses disappointment about the current situation, or a mild reproach/suggestion.
Vて＋もらってもいいですか／いただきたいんですが
Polite, softened request that acknowledges the other person’s effort.
お＋Vます-stem＋いただく／ご＋N＋くださる
Polite expressions for receiving an action or acknowledging someone who does something for you.
てしまう／ておく contractions in polite speech
Distinguish the standard polite forms (てしまいます／ておきます) from casual contractions (ちゃいます／ときます).
Examples from the notes: 会う→お目にかかる; 見せる→お目にかける; 知る→存じ上げる; 思う→存じる.
Honorific pattern for describing the listener’s or another respected person’s state/action; usage depends on the verb and context.
Polite question form used to soften a request or inquiry. Avoid stacking it mechanically after every ますか form.
ていらっしゃる／でいらっしゃる
Respectful form for another person’s ongoing action or state. いらっしゃる refers to people; ございます is used for things or formal self-introduction.
Vさせていただく／くださる
Common polite pattern for doing something with permission; use only when permission or benefit from the other party is relevant.
Vてからでなければ／からでないと
States that the later action is impossible or not allowed before the first action is completed.
かのように／かのような
Describes something as though it were true, often with まるで.
Vない・Vている・A・Nの＋うちに
Do something while a state still holds or before it changes.
Identifies a target audience or intended user group.
Same form family as point 21; meaning is determined by context (agent, means, cause, or variation).
Vている・Nの＋最中に／最中だ
An event occurs during the middle of an ongoing action or period.
Describes an action that has begun but remains incomplete.
Vない＋ずにはいられない／ではいられない
Expresses an irresistible feeling or urge to do something.
Plain form・Aな・Nの＋わけがない
Strongly denies a possibility as unthinkable or unreasonable.
Shows there is no practical alternative.
Emphasizes that the stated reason is especially important.
Can mark an example, belittle something, or express surprise/emotion. The nuance depends on context; it is not limited to a strict noun-versus-verb split.
Strong colloquial impossibility, similar to わけがない.
Often followed by a caution or denial that rejects an automatic conclusion.
Says a general belief or expectation is not always true.
Aい・Aな＋ことといったら
Strongly emphasizes a feeling, impression, or degree.
Often critical or reproachful. Typically used about someone else’s inconsistency.
Describes an impression, tendency, or characteristic (e.g. 子どもっぽい).
せいで attributes an undesirable result to a cause; せいか presents the cause as uncertain.
Knowing …; knowing the kind of person …
Uses what is known about someone to make a likely prediction.
Often describes a slight, usually temporary condition such as 疲れ気味 or 寝不足気味.
Vて＋なんかいない／なんかいられない
I’m not … at all / can’t afford to …
なんか／なんて adds emphasis: denial in the first pattern, inability to continue/allow in the second.
Emphasizes an extreme or surprising example; the particle before さえ depends on the noun’s role.
To the extent that; at least
Can show degree or a minimum expectation. せめて often adds ‘at least’ as a wish or complaint.
Marks an action or state left unattended or continuing longer than appropriate. The form is っぱなし, not っぽなし.
Covered with; full of (usually undesirable things)
Often used with dirt, mistakes, or other things viewed negatively.
Can make a tentative or light guess, or gently describe unexpected behavior; distinguish this from listing actions with ～たり～たりする.
Describes qualities that seem typical of a person, season, or group.
The initial impression or expectation is quickly overturned by what follows.
とか can list examples or casually report information; the role depends on the sentence.
While you’re at it; on the occasion of
Adds a secondary action done during an opportunity created by the main action.
Plain form・Aな・N＋に違いない／に相違ない
Must be; there is no doubt
Strong inference or conviction. に相違ない is more formal.
Emphasizes that something is unsurpassed in a particular context.
Says something is omitted or excluded.
Vて・Aくて・Aで＋しょうがない
Expresses an intense feeling or state that is hard to control. Also written しようがない.

sourceNotes.note: Godan verbs may have a contracted causative-passive: 読む→読ませられる／読まされる. Ichidan 食べる stays 食べさせられる; する becomes させられる.
The pattern is ～られてしまう (しまう), not ～られてしまる.
The examples 読んどく／調べとく are contractions of ておく, not ていく.
Use ～たりして for the light guess (e.g. 高かったりして); the formation is not simply ‘past form + りして’.
Clause-linking examples like 実施し、まとめる use the ます-stem/連用形, not the て-form.
The standard form is ～っぱなし. It can describe a neglected state (e.g. leaving something on) or an action that continues, often with a negative nuance.
